recipes.name: Squash Casserole with Cream of Chicken Soup
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds yellow crookneck squash - peeled, seeded, and sliced
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup
7.5 ounces herbed dry bread stuffing mix

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Cook squash and onions in boiling salted water until tender. Drain and mash them with 1/2 cup butter or margarine. Stir in sour cream, grated carrot and cream of chicken soup. Set aside.

Melt remaining 1/2 cup butter and stir it into the stuffing mix. Pour half of the stuffing mix into the bottom of a 9X13 glass baking pan. Pour the squash mixture over the top of the mixture, and the rest of the stuffing mix on top of the squash.
Bake for 30 minutes, until golden brown and bubbly.

raw_recipe.headline: Squash Casserole with Cream of Chicken Soup
raw_recipe.description: Crookneck squash, cream of chicken soup, and veggies are topped with herbed stuffing mix for a creamy, crunchy side dish casserole.

review.reviewBody: My family loves this dish! I didn't peel or mash the squash but sliced/quartered it and I didn't use the butter. Used reduced fat sour cream to lower the calorie count as we're watching our diets. Used Vidalia onion and cut into bite sized pieces for extra flavor. Also used cream of mushroom soup and I'm going to try cream of celery soup next time to see how it tastes. I also have blended zucchini and yellow squash for a different look to the dish sometimes. This dish gets thumbs up everywhere I take it. Great way to use the garden goodies!!!

So impressed with this idea. I am sure it's great as written, so 5 stars. I used a little olive oil and black pepper to saute the mixed yellow squash and zucchini I had until fairly tender. Also had the thin sliced onion in there as well. I cheated for time and used my salad shooter to shoot them right into the pan! Used the can of chicken soup and 1/4 cup of sour cream. Had a box of instant turkey stuffing, bcs we were having turkey fillets, and mixed a melted stick of butter (half cup) in it until a little browned. Mixed half of it into the squash mixture once most of the liquid was evaporated, topped it with the rest, and in 25 minutes had an amazing casserole. My apologies for making changes to the originator, bcs I am sure it was fantastic that way also. I did borrow from some of the other commentators, so thank you. This will be my go to squash casserole from now on!

Have made a few times, wash, cut and quarter squash, no need to peel or seed or cook. Put into crockpot with rest of ingredients and dry chicken stovetop stuffing with herbs as well as some shredded chicken. Let cook on low for about 6 hours. Stir occasionally. Comes out creamy and tasty.

Second time making this recipe. I sautee the squash and onion on olive oil. I dont skin or remove seeds from the squash and vidalia onion is best for this casserole. Turns out perfect. I do add a bit of shredded four cheese blend. Melting the butter a bit helps coat the stuffing, and I double the stuffing. One pouch is not enough for me. Lovely dish.!

My family and I have been making this exact recipe for years at Thanksgiving, so I know it is amazing! This recipe is the reason I don't like to try other squash casseroles -- honestly, the other ones I have tried NEVER stack up! Things I do differently: I don't peel or seed my squash. I cut the squash instead into about 1/4 to 1/2 inch thick slices before boiling, and I do not mash them after boiling -- I just put the slices in the casserole. It tastes delicious this way, although I imagine mashing is good for tricking picky eaters. Another good tip -- you can swap out yellow squash for zucchini in this recipe, or do half and half for some variety and color -- the taste is about the same. Delicious!

Everyone loved it, I was hesitant based on the previous reviews but it came out great. I liked the breadcrumbs more than the ritz crackers. Instead of using one cup of sour cream I did 1/2 so it didn't overpower the dish and it was good.

I got some free squash and zucchini from a co-worker and found this recipe to try out. I did a few things different. I quartered the squash and zucchini and sauted them with the onions in olive oil and garlic. I didn't mash them but put the chunks in with the soup/sour cream mixture and added a can of Rotel. The Rotel gave the dish the flavor some other reviewers complained was lacking. My husband said he would have this almost vegetarian dish anytime.

I’ve made similar recipes before but this is still a delicious, filling, meatless Monday dish! The only change was sautéd the squash and onions vs boiled and didn’t mash them with the butter - thus reducing the fat a bit. Ate with freshly baked bread and this was a comfort food meal! Thank you!

We have used this recipe for about 20 years, it's older than that! Pepperidge Farm stuffing mix, the "crumb" style is best. If you only find the bread cubes, smash w a mallet in a zip lock bag. For vegetarians, any Cream of vegetable soup works. Cream of Mushroom is our alternate fav! Even people that dislike zucchini or yellow squash will enjoy the dish!
This is a "family recipe" that we have been making for years. Our recipe calls for 2 lb of squash instead of 1 1/2. One trick is to drain the squash VERY well so the casserole sets up. Delicious.

I love squash and wanted something yummy besides fried squash. My neighbor gave me this recipe to try and it is AMAZING!

The only change I did make was adding grated cheese to the recipe to make it cheesy and kid friendly! One hint I would like to give is -- instead of boiling the squash and onion, sautee it in olive oil for 10-15 minutes. This gives the dish a better flavor and the squash isn't as mushy!
Very easy and delicious!
Easy peasy, used fat free cream of chicken soup. It's delicious.
Perfect recipe. My family loves this!
Loved this recipe. I kept the veges whole did not mash a d added upon gold rough chop potatoes to the mix. Now one of my go to fav. Recipes!!!!.

The stuffing mix adds lots of flavor and crunch. Can use crushed Ritz crackers tho if don’t have/like stuffing mix. I have made this for years and have learned to steam the squash (and 1/2 onion too) and then drain for a couple hours to get as much water out as possible. Boiling makes too watery. IF you don’t like sour cream, use 1/2 c mayo instead, and add 1 c shredded cheddar cheese to the mix too. My aunt adds 1 T minced fresh sage and it adds such a great taste so I always add that now. Sometimes I add a small can of drained chopped water chestnuts, too, for a little texture in the casserole. Good either way. Any way you fix this, it is a very good use of summer squash!
I sautéed the vegetables together then used cream of celery soup instead of cream of chicken. Delicious
Substituted strained yogurt for sour cream. Used half the amount of butter. Used extra amount of squash and onions.
Oh my gosh, the first dish I ever learned how to make was squash casserole but a very simple recipe this one by far is the BEST. It is so creamy and full of flavor just my old recipe will be trashed!
A little too creamy to suit us so will increase amount of squash and/or decrease the sour cream next time but still very tasty.
